Core rules for gate calls
Everyone on the desk should know how the desk handles it
Companion Animal Travel Desk Rules
This section sets the standard for calm, careful handling of companion animal travel from booking review through pickup, with safety and clear records placed before speed at every step. When a gate call affects a traveler with a companion animal, the desk should respond at once, confirm the passenger record, and keep the handoff orderly so the animal remains secure and the traveler receives steady guidance. Staff should use plain language, listen closely, and document every change in the file so later staff can trace what was said and what was done.

If a delay or other irregular service creates a support claim, the record must be complete before it moves forward. <<FACT F109>> The desk should then note the service conditions, advise the traveler with courtesy, and avoid promises that are not already authorized. Where a traveler presents more than one concern, the senior coordinator should separate the animal-care issue from the baggage or ticket matter and route each item to the proper team. Any handling of Louie or another animal must remain gentle, quiet, and consistent with the approved travel plan, and staff should verify carrier condition, relief needs, and loading status before release at the gate.

If a passenger must be reassigned to another counter or escorted to another point of contact, the handoff should be complete, respectful, and written down. The desk should preserve all notes in the case file, including spoken updates that affect boarding, delivery, or pickup. When uncertainty remains, the agent should pause and seek guidance rather than guess, because a clear record protects the traveler, the animal, and Aurelia Skyways.

For any unresolved animal-travel matter, contact the senior coordinator or the duty supervisor at the Companion Animal Travel Desk.
